I've been considering a solar setup. Is it worth it? And how hard is it? Is this something you did yourself?

The return of a solar system has a lot to do with your location. If you live down south somewhere with a lot of sun, it's a great investment. If you live up north where days are short and the sun comes in at a low angle, less so.

For most folks, solar systems are going to take 5-10 years before they've paid for themselves in power reduction. But the value of having an emergency system in place that you can rely on is much more difficult to put a price tag on.

There are some US subsidy programs (check your local state as well) that can help offset the costs of a solar system. Essentially you have two choices:

  • Let some solar contractor come in and install everything. They'll charge you a bunch, but it'll be set up right.
  • Do a shit ton of research and buy the parts individually and install it yourself. It's cheaper, but only works if you're not a fuckup.

I decided to go the cheaper route. It turns out, for my area the roof angle was pretty close to a good panel installation angle so we just slapped them right on top. This isn't as consistent as the tracking platforms, but I didn't like the idea of all those moving parts. I'm happy to take a 15% loss in performance if it means I never have to worry about a tracking servo getting stuck or stripped out by wind.

Currently we don't have it hooked into the grid 24/7, but it's because I'm taking my time in learning the electrical side of things. I have four 12V batteries that the solar panels keep topped up - which is more than enough power to do simple stuff like charge phones and AAs, or run a power inverter for a little while.

My goal is to keep the essentials running: the freezer, furnace, and water pump. Our electrical, like most homes, is not exactly set up for a quick changeover when the grid goes down so it's going to be a rewiring project to get them all on a single circuit I can get an inverter connected to.
